text:
Tampa Bay's three-game winning streak ended in Denver, and it ended with the Lightning doing most of the things a winning team does. TBL lost 6-3 to COL, despite taking 76 shot attempts to Colorado's 47 and out-chancing the Avalanche 3.95 to 2.92 in expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances. By the odds of simulated replays of every shot, TBL deserved to win 75 percent of the time.

The gap came down to finishing and goaltending. Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed 5 goals on 23 shots, about 2.6 more than the quality of those shots deserved, a number known as goals saved above expected. Mackenzie Blackwood, at the other end, stopped 31 of 34 and came out 0.95 goals ahead of expectation, including a 33 percent chance from Brayden Point in the first period. Devon Toews opened the scoring at 1:08 on a 5 percent chance, and Nazem Kadri made it 2-0 on the power play. Fedor Svechkov pushed it to 3-0 early in the second, even as TBL took over that period 2.13 to 0.87 in expected goals. Jake Guentzel scored twice, once on the power play and once with 43 seconds left in the second, but Artturi Lehkonen had already made it 4-1.

Nathan MacKinnon finished with a goal and three assists, and Martin Necas added a goal and two assists, scoring the sixth after Charle-Edouard D'Astous had cut it to 5-3 late in the third. The facts supply no records or standings for either club, but the Lightning will carry a loss they largely outplayed into their next game, while Colorado took the points on the strength of timely scoring and its goalie.
